name: Raw markup renders into styled type

source.description: 1 inspected reference film (batch-2, 2026-11-26): an editor launch types raw markup in monospace and re-sets it into the display serif, showing input become output.

technique: Raw source text with its markup symbols types in monospace, then the symbols drop away and the word re-sets in the display face: the viewer sees input become output. Works for markdown, code and formulas.
purpose: Show input becoming output: syntax, code or a formula turning into what it produces.
visual_behaviour: Raw source text with its markup symbols types in monospace behind a block caret; the symbols drop away and the word re-sets in the display face, passing briefly through a scrambled mix.
mechanics: Monospace typing with a block caret at about 10 characters/s (ref-3abcbedd20: the heading marker and first letter at 0.39 s, the whole word at 0.87 s); the swap to the serif passes through a scrambled mix (1.12 s) and lands by 1.88 s; the second line types with an emphasis marker and re-sets as the italic accent line (2.04-4.12 s). Accents on keystrokes. Swap mechanics not pinned (no 30 fps strip of 0.8-1.9 s).
failure_modes: A slow swap looks like a font-loading bug

implementation.approach: Studio.type.typewriter at about 10 characters/s with a block caret for the raw line; then hide the markup characters and swap the word to the display face through a seeded scramble (text-scramble-decode) of about 0.3-1.0 s. The swap mechanics were not pinned frame by frame (no 30 fps strip of 0.8-1.9 s).

provenance.observed: A heading typed in monospace with its markup re-sets as a serif headline; the second line does the same into italic.

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
